- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.7) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop — add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — apply 2–5% downward adjustment to first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -1.0 to -1.95), model tends to ignore mean reversion — force 3–5 day mean-reversion correction toward prior 10-day average.
- If model forecast is >+10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–15% if sentiment is flat or negative — avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
